title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-05-05
content:
Perf & Benchmarking sync notes — 2026-05-05

Attendees:
- Asha Patel (owner)
- Miguel Torres
- Zoe Chen
- Liam O'Connor
- Priya Nair (notes)

Goals for this sync:
- Triage the p95/p99 latency regressions observed in last week's nightly runs.
- Review recent test runs for rwd-open-7b-quant and rwd-open-13b (cpu/gpu combos).
- Align on immediate mitigations and next experiments.

Summary / tl;dr:
- We have a reproducible latency regression on rwd-open-7b-quant (GPU) for short-context workloads (<=64 tokens) when batch_size=1: p95 went from ~120ms (baseline, 2026-04-28) to ~310ms (2026-05-04).
- Regression correlates to kernel selection change introduced in commit 9b3f4a2 (kernel fallback heuristics).
- Throughput for large batch sizes (bs>=16) is unaffected; end-to-end tail spikes are isolated to small-batch interactive paths.
- Immediate mitigation: roll back the heuristic in canary and re-run nightly; longer-term: refine heuristic and add microbenchmark gating.

Notes from test runs (all runs in CI cluster gwp-prod-sim):
- Baseline (2026-04-28): rwd-open-7b-quant, GPU A100, batch_size=1, seq_len=32, p50=55ms, p95=120ms, p99=210ms.
- Recent failing run (2026-05-04): same infra, p50=60ms, p95=310ms, p99=540ms.
- Canary with commit 9b3f4a2 reverted (run 2026-05-05 03:10): p95=128ms (back to baseline range).
- rwd-open-13b (GPU) shows mild increase in p95 (~10%), but not as pronounced; suggests change impacts quantized path more.
- CPU-hosted tests: no measurable regression (p95 stable), which points to GPU kernel selection logic as root cause.

Key observations:
- Regression only triggers when continuous-batching queue is empty (i.e., interactive single-request flows).
- Profiling (NVIDIA Nsight + runtime traces) shows extra kernel-launch overhead and an extra memcpy in the hot path when heuristic chooses fallback kernel.
- Heuristic update attempted to prefer a "unified" kernel for small sequence lengths to improve generic throughput — unintended side-effect: increased branching and extra copy for some weight layouts (seen in quantized kernels).

Hypotheses to validate:
1) The heuristic incorrectly classifies some quantized weight layouts as "non-compat" and forces a slower kernel path.
2) JIT/kernel warmup introduced in 9b3f4a2 has a higher fixed-cost for first few requests; combined with single-request interaction leads to visible p95 increase.
3) Small difference in CUDA stream synchronization ordering triggers additional implicit synchronizations for quantized kernels.

Immediate actions agreed:
- ACTION-1 (owner: Miguel) — Revert heuristic in canary pool and monitor 24h: job id run-canary-2026-05-05-08. Target: confirm p95 returns to baseline. Due: 2026-05-06.
- ACTION-2 (owner: Zoe) — Add microbenchmark that isolates kernel-selection path (unit test + perf harness) and add to pre-merge CI. PR: linked PR 754. Due: 2026-05-12.
- ACTION-3 (owner: Liam) — Instrument runtime to emit a small metric when fallback kernel is selected (counts + last-selected-kernel-id). Add to logs for the next 3 days. Due: 2026-05-07.
- ACTION-4 (owner: Priya) — Collect full Nsight profile for failing run and attach to Confluence page. Due: 2026-05-06.

Longer-term experiments / follow-ups:
- Experiment: refine heuristic to include a quick weight-layout fingerprint (cheap) to avoid misclassification. Miguel + Zoe to prototype.
- Gate: add microbenchmark gating in CI; PRs that change kernel-selection or fallback heuristics must show no >5% p95 regression on quantized small-batch interactive tests.
- Explore opportunistic pre-warming for hot paths in canary pools to mitigate first-request JIT cost.

Risks / customer impact:
- Interactive use-cases (chat UIs) routed to hosted API could see tail latency blips — estimated exposure currently low (~2% of traffic hits the quantized-small-batch path).
- Dedicated customers pinning quantized variants may see regressions if on versions with 9b3f4a2. Notifying major Dedicated customers is recommended if rollback not quick.

Decisions made:
- Revert on canary started immediately (Miguel).
- Add CI microbenchmark before merging heuristic rework (Zoe + Miguel).

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we need to introduce a versioned kernel catalog so runtime picks kernels based on model+quantization profile and not heuristics? (parking for architecture discussion)
- Should we add a per-model metric for kernel-selection to the Console for easier debugging by customer support?

Next meeting:
- Follow-up sync: 2026-05-07 10:30 PT (quick check-in) — focus: canary metrics and instrumentation outputs.
- Full retrospective and post-mortem (if regression confirmed across more models): 2026-05-12 11:00 PT.

Appendix: quick checklist for rollback verification
- Confirm canary p95 for rwd-open-7b-quant back to <=160ms (Miguel).
- Verify no increase in GPU utilization for batch_size=1 workloads after revert (Liam).
- Confirm no related regressions on rwd-open-13b (Zoe).

Notes to self (informal):
- We should automate the correlation between kernel-selection changes and p95 deltas across nightly runs. Right now it's manual and slow.
- Remember to include PR link in customer-facing post if we need to notify Dedicated customers.

End of notes.

Recorded by: Priya Nair
